entries.name: GitHub Spec Kit
entries.summary: Structured development processes and templates, with an explicitly documented IBM Bob integration.
notes: The documented Bob integration uses .bob/skills/speckit-<command>/SKILL.md by default.
The integration guide distinguishes current skills from the deprecated Bob 1.x commands layout.

sources.supports: Public source, project purpose, installation instructions, and repository license.
IBM Bob integration key, skills layout, invocation, and legacy migration.

entries.name: IBM Bob Workshops
entries.summary: Workshop source and exercises covering Bob usage, rules, skills, MCP, and team workflows.
notes: Contains an agent-with-bob-shell skill alongside workshop materials.
Different labs have different audiences; the power-user workshop targets IBM employees.

sources.supports: Public files, workshop scope, audience, and Apache-2.0 license.
Power-user exercises for rules, skills, MCP, and team workflows.

entries.name: IBM Bob Demos
entries.summary: Task examples for skills, documentation indexing, architecture, modernization, and DevOps.
notes: The reviewed README still names earlier modes such as Code, Advanced, and Orchestrator.
The repository describes itself as an open-source project rather than a supported IBM product.

sources.supports: Examples, clone instructions, older mode names, license, and public-repository support disclosure.

entries.name: Bob+ Technology Building Blocks
entries.summary: IBM Build Engineering reference implementations, integration assets, and Bob skills and modes.
notes: A public skills ZIP is visible; its contents were not executed.
VSIX installation is documented, but this review did not verify a downloadable VSIX package.

sources.supports: Public source, project scope, and Apache-2.0 license.
Skills installation locations and domain coverage.
Documented VSIX installation workflow, not runtime verification.

entries.name: bob-skill-installer
entries.summary: A community Python tool for fetching, converting, validating, and installing third-party skills into Bob.
notes: Documents project/global targets, dry runs, and upgrade backups.
Its documented default preserves source secret files unless excluded; inspect options before use.

sources.supports: Public Python implementation, installation options, secret-file behavior, and license.

entries.name: OnboardOps
entries.summary: A community onboarding workflow combining Bob instructions, skills, an MCP server, and a repository-learning dashboard.
notes: The README identifies the project as a Bob hackathon submission.
Treat its custom-mode representation as project-specific until checked against the installed Bob version.

sources.supports: Public source, onboarding components, hackathon origin, and MIT license.

entries.name: Debug Swarm
entries.summary: A community debugging workflow with focused investigators, run artifacts, a dashboard, and a planted-bug benchmark.
notes: The repository documents a seven-phase debugging skill and replayable reference runs.
Upstream test counts and benchmark outcomes have not been independently reproduced by this catalogue.

sources.supports: Public source, workflow components, quick-start instructions, and MIT license.
